name: layout/flex
description: Flex layout primitive for vertical or horizontal stacking with gap control. ⚠ Unlike CSS `flex-direction`, `direction` defaults to `vertical` — pass `direction="horizontal"` for a row.

meta.name: Flex
meta.description: Flex layout primitive for vertical or horizontal stacking with gap control. ⚠ Unlike CSS `flex-direction`, `direction` defaults to `vertical` — pass `direction="horizontal"` for a row.

props.name: direction
props.description: Flex direction. ⚠ Defaults to `vertical`, unlike CSS `flex-direction` (and unlike Chakra/MUI/Radix `Flex`, which default to a row) — `<Flex justify="between">` alone produces a centered vertical stack.

props.name: size
props.description: FlexItem: main-axis sizing. 'fixed' (flex: 0 0 auto) is what a fixed-width child like Sparkline needs; 'grow' takes the leftover width without shrinking; 'shrink' gives way but never grows.

props.name: basis
props.description: FlexItem: flex-basis — the child's size before free space is distributed. Any CSS length.

props.name: truncate
props.description: FlexItem: allow the child to shrink below its content width (releases the flex item's `min-width: auto` floor and ellipsizes). Without it a long unbreakable string pushes its siblings out of the row.

examples.title: Toolbar: one field absorbs the row, the rest keep their width
examples.code:
<Flex direction="horizontal" gap={2}>
  <FlexItem size="grow" basis="0"><Search ariaLabel="Filter deployments" /></FlexItem>
  <FlexItem size="fixed"><Select options={states} ariaLabel="State" /></FlexItem>
</Flex>
examples.description: Without FlexItem the Search takes the whole row and pushes the Select onto the next line

examples.title: Protecting a fixed-width child
examples.code:
<Flex direction="horizontal" gap={3} align="center">
  <FlexItem truncate>{deployment.url}</FlexItem>
  <FlexItem size="fixed"><Sparkline data={points} label="Requests" /></FlexItem>
</Flex>
examples.description: Sparkline is fixed-width and will not shrink; `size="fixed"` keeps it out of flex sizing, `truncate` lets the URL beside it ellipsize instead of pushing it out

whenToUse: Arranging children vertically or horizontally with a consistent gap
The default primitive for spacing a small set of elements in one direction
whenNotToUse: Responsive auto-wrapping card collections — use AutoGrid
A visual card-pile / overlapping avatars — that is `Stack` in @cascivo/react (an `offset` prop), a different component.

antiPatterns.bad: Expecting import { Stack } from '@cascivo/react' to gap items
antiPatterns.good: Use Flex for gap-based layout (import { Flex } from "@cascivo/react", or `npx cascivo add flex`)
antiPatterns.why: The published `Stack` export is a card-pile that overlaps children by an offset — it does not do gap-based layout. Flex is the flex container.

related.name: Stack
related.reason: The `@cascivo/react` `Stack` overlaps children with an offset (card-pile) — a different component for visual overlap, not gap-based layout.

intent.a11yRationale: Pure layout primitive with no semantic role; does not affect the accessibility tree.
